in science, it is acting on a theory that may fail tomorrow"]}, "claim": "Popper's preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on his own terms as a non-inductive 'critical preference' based on verisimilitude (truth-likeness), but accepting this costs the ability to ever claim rational certainty that the preferred theory is true or even probably true;
